title: Atomistic insights into hydrogen diffusion mechanisms, multi-step dehydrogenation, and strain-engineered thermodynamics in orthorhombic ternary magnesium hydrides
content: Solid-state complex hydrides offer a promising solution for safe hydrogen storage, yet practical applications remain constrained by high thermodynamic stability and sluggish kinetics. In this study, orthorhombic strontium magnesium tetrahydride (SrMgH4, space group Cmc21) was investigated using Density Functional Theory (DFT). SrMgH4 exhibits mechanical stability via Born criteria, dynamic lattice stability from phonon dispersion, and a wide bandgap of Eg = 2.836 eV (3.801 eV via the HSE06 hybrid functional). It delivers a theoretical gravimetric capacity of 3.48 wt% and an outstanding volumetric density of 88.18 g H2 per L. From a kinetic perspective, the LST/QST method predicts that SrMgH4 has fast diffusion pathways with energy barriers as low as 0.242 eV along the H3–H4 path, and an interconnected 3D percolating network (≤0.482 eV). It is predicted that the single-step decomposition of SrMgH4 would require a desorption temperature of 768 K in its undeformed state. However, an intermediate pathway via the binary compound SrH2 significantly lowers the desorption temperature to 546 K. Additionally, applying a triaxial strain of −4% to −5% lowers the desorption temperature to 345.0 K, making it within the goals of the US Department of Energy (DOE). These results indicate that SrMgH4 is an excellent material for reversible solid state hydrogen storage.
